title: perf(canary): ship steady-state canary pipeline + rollout-guard integration
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: shipping model or runtime changes without continuous guardrails has resulted in two production regressions in the last quarter. This PR introduces a continuous performance-canary pipeline that runs steady-state microbenchmarks and short ramp tests against staged model/runtime variants, computes a composite canary score (latency p50/p95/p99 + throughput stability + error rate), and wires automated rollout-guard actions into the Redwood Console. The goal is to detect sustained regressions early (nightly/scheduled + on-PR short runs) and block automated rollouts until regressions are triaged.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new perf-canary service and pipeline: scripts and a GH Actions job (.github/workflows/perf-canary.yml) to execute microbenchmarks against a canary environment and baseline.
- Implements a canary scoring library (scripts/perf_canary/score.py) that computes composite scores using weighted percentiles and a simple Bayesian uplift check to avoid noisy false positives.
- Integrates the canary runner with Redwood Console: canary results are sent to the new /api/internal/canary endpoint; console shows pass/fail and time-series.
- Rollout guard controller (controllers/rollout_guard.go): subscribes to canary results, enforces per-deployment threshold policies, and can (1) pause a rollout, (2) rollback to previous model snapshot, and (3) open a Linear ticket automatically when configured.
- Alerting hooks: Prometheus metrics (metrics/perf_canary.prom), Grafana dashboard panels (observability/dashboards/canary.jsonnet), and Slack notifications for degradations.
- E2E smoke + integration tests for the runner and controller (integration/perf_canary_test.go).
- Docs and runbook: docs/perf-canary.md + runbooks/incident-perf-canary.md.

Checklist: [x] perf runner + scoring library added, [x] CI job + scheduling, [x] console endpoint + UI hook, [x] rollout controller + policy config, [x] metrics + dashboards, [x] tests, [x] docs.

Notes on design and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally run a mix of short PR-level runs (3min, synthetic traffic) and longer scheduled steady-state runs (30–60min) to catch both regressions in startup/steady-state and throughput tail behavior.
- Composite canary score is conservative by default; teams can opt-in to stricter policies at deployment time via deployment.yaml -> rolloutGuard section.
- We added a small amount of latency to the console API path to avoid blocking the control plane on canary analysis; results are posted asynchronously and control decisions are made by the rollout controller which reads canonical results from Prometheus + the internal canary store.

Migration / rollout plan: enable default nightly canary job for most services in staging first; expose policy toggles in the UI; after two weeks of low-noise results, flip on canary enforcement for select services.

Related: Linear ENG-873 (perf canary spec), ENG-912 (rollout guard API), ENG-995 (console canary UI).

release_notes: Adds a continuous performance canary pipeline, console canary UI, and rollout guard controller. Enables automated detection of latency/throughput regressions and configurable rollout enforcement. Default: nightly canaries in staging; enforcement opt-in per-service.
